summary: Bounded yt-dlp's related-track lookup with a 20s socket timeout, so a slow or contended extraction can no longer stall a thread-pool slot indefinitely during autoplay.
details: Diagnosed a live 'autoplay is NOT working' report (2026-09-02): the queue emptying and staying empty (idle disconnect) had no log line distinguishing WHY -- autoplay disabled, no seed track, or a related() call that came back empty/slow. Added logging at each of those decision points, plus timing on the live related() call.

A single related() Mix extraction measured 20-31s under concurrent load against the shared YoutubeDL instance (vs. single digits idle) -- and cancelling the asyncio Task awaiting it does not stop the underlying thread. Both yt-dlp option sets now carry socket_timeout=20 so a stuck request fails fast and logged instead of pinning an executor thread.
limitations: The exact mechanism behind the reported failure is not yet confirmed -- this lands the instrumentation needed to pin it down on the next occurrence, plus a defensive bound on the one measured anomaly (abnormal extraction latency).
